_comment: Declarative manifest of INSTALLABLE (dynamic) vessels — the single source of truth for vessel-ctl.sh install/uninstall. Built-in vessels are baked into the image; this file is for vessels added/removed at runtime (federation, future). Each vessel: name (== systemd unit name), workdir (run dir; supports $REPO_ROOT), exec (bun entrypoint, relative to workdir), env (STATIC literal Environment= lines), secrets (keys from secrets.env.sh that must be in /etc/substrate/env — supplied to the unit via EnvironmentFile, NOT Environment=), restart, health_port (for /health + self-recovery), self_recovery (add to self-recovery-tick VESSELS), post_install (optional shell run after start, e.g. capture a dynamic relay multiaddr into /etc/substrate/env).

vessels.name: metric-collector-vessel
vessels.description: Substrate-authored sample collector (metricSample shapes; lift empirical test).

vessels.name: human-surface-vessel
vessels.description: Human-facing surface vessel — the UI a human resolver talks to; the only vessel a UI-only federated spoke needs to serve locally.
vessels._host_comment: HOST is 0.0.0.0 because this vessel exists to be reached by a human from OUTSIDE the container. render-unit.sh emits these env lines AFTER EnvironmentFile=/etc/substrate/env, so whatever is written here wins. A 127.0.0.1 bind does not accept the DNAT'd traffic a `docker run -p` publish delivers from the container's bridge IP, so the host port mapping exists and is dead — the vessel answers /health in-container and nothing on the host. stateful-ui-vessel, which this vessel replaces, sets 0.0.0.0 for the same reason. Registration is unaffected: the discovery payload uses SELF_ENDPOINT = http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (src/config.ts), a constant independent of HOST.
vessels._post_install_comment: SKIPS THE BUILD WHEN dist CAME FROM GIT, and that guard is load-bearing. ui/dist is now TRACKED, because the substrate updates itself by pulling and nothing rebuilds on pull — git is the delivery channel. A rebuild does not reproduce the committed bundle byte-for-byte (vite content-hashes, and the container's bun differs from the operator's: the same source produced CN--oDvm, Y3nhnr7c, CIgDXFb9 and aOP5YrJ- on four machines), so building over a tracked dist leaves MODIFIED tracked files, `git pull --ff-only` then refuses, and the vessel silently stops converging to origin/dev. That is the same wedge that stranded the hub's development-vessel 124 commits behind. Build ONLY when dist is absent — a fork building from a tree that predates the tracked bundle, or a source-only checkout. vessel-ctl runs `bun install` ONLY in the rendered WorkingDirectory (the server), never a build. Paths are LITERAL: post_install is handed to the container shell verbatim, so $REPO_ROOT/$RUNTIME are NOT expanded here (federation-relay's hook is literal for the same reason). HOME and the bun cache dir are pinned OUTSIDE the repo: a HOME redirected into the tree leaked a 146MB bun cache into it. vessel-ctl SWALLOWS this hook's stdout, stderr AND exit status (`csh "$post" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`), so the hook writes its own log and a terminal OK/FAILED sentinel — that log is the only evidence a build failed, and callers should assert ui/dist exists rather than trust the install's ok:true.
vessels.post_install: L=/workspace/human-surface-ui-build.log; D=/workspace/git/super-repo/repos/human-surface-vessel/ui/dist; if [ -f "$D/index.html" ]; then echo "UI_BUILD_SKIPPED (dist came from git — rebuilding would dirty tracked files and wedge pull-sync)" > "$L"; else { export HOME=/root; export BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/root/.bun/install/cache; set -x; cd /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/human-surface-vessel/ui && /root/.bun/bin/bun install && /root/.bun/bin/bun run build && test -d dist; } > "$L" 2>&1 && echo UI_BUILD_OK >> "$L" || echo UI_BUILD_FAILED >> "$L"; fi

vessels.name: federation-relay
vessels.description: Public libp2p Circuit Relay v2 — the from-anywhere reachability anchor.
vessels.post_install: for i in $(seq 1 20); do m=$(grep -m1 'RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /workspace/fed-relay.log 2>/dev/null | sed 's/RELAY_MULTIADDR=//'); [ -n "$m" ] && { grep -v '^RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /etc/substrate/env > /etc/substrate/env.tmp && mv /etc/substrate/env.tmp /etc/substrate/env; echo "RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m" >> /etc/substrate/env; echo "captured RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m"; break; }; sleep 1; done

vessels.name: federation-transport-vessel
vessels.description: libp2p reachability + cross-substrate resolve-over-http + /health sensing surface.
